Oct 29 : Spaniard Jorge Martin has been cleared to take part in Friday's opening practice session at the Malaysian Grand Prix after passing a medical examination on the wrist injury he suffered in a crash at Phillip Island, Aprilia said on Thursday. Martin fractured his right wrist during a sprint race battle with title rival Marc Marquez in Australia and was ruled out of the main race, which was later cancelled due to heavy rain and poor visibility. Martin is 10 points adrift of Ducati's Marquez in the MotoGP standings with four rounds remaining. "Martin will be out on track in the opening stint of a crucial grand prix in the ever-changing 2026 title race," Aprilia said in a statement.

Oct 29 : Nasdaq futures dropped on Thursday as mixed earnings from Alphabet and Microsoft left investors weighing the payoff from heavy AI spending, with focus also on an inflation reading a day after the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged. Alphabet slid 10.5 per cent in premarket trading after the company reported disappointing results in the core business of search advertising and a massive acceleration in cash burn as it poured resources into building out AI. "Investors are starting to scrutinize monetization timelines versus the capital expenditure burn rates. Some investors are no longer giving all hyperscalers a 'free pass' to spend without limit," said Jeremy Saltzberg, VP and senior investment officer at Check Capital Management. On the other hand, Microsoft climbed 3.5 per cent after the company delivered a big cash-flow beat and forecast strong cloud growth, offering fresh evidence that its hefty AI bets were working.

Other early movers included cybersecurity firm Fortinet, which tumbled 25.4 per cent after reporting third-quarter results. Software maker ServiceNow dropped 19 per cent after missing third-quarter profit estimates. Other software-related companies, including Zscaler and Salesforce, were among the laggards in sector-wide weakness. Marvell Technology fell 9.4 per cent after media reports said the company is in advanced talks to buy data-center optics maker Lumentum Holdings. Lumentum shares rose 4.3 per cent. Marvell and Lumentum did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. The broader semiconductor space was trading lower, with Nvidia down 1 per cent, AMD sliding 3.3 per cent and Intel off 3.6 per cent. Intel and Amazon are some of the major tech companies reporting after markets close on Thursday. On the earnings docket before the bell are drugmakers Merck and Eli Lilly, construction equipment maker Caterpillar, and alternative investment managers Ares Management and Blue Owl. At 4:09 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 185 points, or 0.35 per cent, and S&P 500 E-minis were down 31 points, or 0.41 per cent. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 365 points, or 1.22 per cent. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday, as expected, opting to delay any changes to borrowing costs until after next week's US midterm elections while it awaits further data on inflation. "The decision to hold seems to be a short pause to assess ahead of a likely policy hike in December, rather than an indication that no further tightening is needed," said Jon Butcher, a senior US economist at Aberdeen. Focus will be on the September Personal Consumption Expenditures report, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, due later in the day. A third-quarter GDP reading is also set for release. Traders currently see a more than 81 per cent chance the Fed will hike interest rates in December, as per the CME FedWatch Tool, as key inflation metrics remain elevated amid the oil shock caused by the Middle East conflict. Money market participants are also pricing an additional rate hike by mid-2027, according to data compiled by LSEG. Among other stocks, car e-commerce platform Carvana jumped 9.2 per cent after its third-quarter revenue surpassed estimates, while Chipotle Mexican Grill gained 6.7 per cent after reporting better-than-expected quarterly comparable sales.

Source: Reuters

Oct 29 : Jordan Football Association chief Prince Ali bin Hussein said he will cooperate with any Asian Football Confederation judicial review after he accused FIFA President Gianni Infantino of hijacking last week's AFC Congress for political purposes. AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al-Khalifa had endorsed Infantino for reelection at the continental body's extraordinary congress in Tokyo. Following the meeting, Prince Ali alleged delegates had not been allowed to speak, question or debate matters and described the final day of the congress as "pure politics at the behest of Gianni Infantino". FIFA did not respond to a Reuters request for comment on Prince Ali's remarks.

The AFC said on Tuesday that neither Prince Ali nor any other member association's representatives had requested to speak and that allegations involving coercion, threats or bribery should be supported by credible evidence. It added that it would refer Prince Ali's statements to its judicial bodies. "I respect the AFC and its judicial bodies and will cooperate fully with any process," Prince Ali said in a post on X late on Wednesday. "As the FIFA Statutes provide, the Jordan Football Association will cast its vote in the FIFA presidential election independently." He said his earlier post about the congress was intended to explain the FIFA presidential voting process and highlight the importance of transparency in football governance. "Its final sentence states a principle the whole football family shares: no election should be open to coercion, threats or bribery. I stand by that principle. It was a statement of principle, not an allegation against any person," he said. "Where concerns arise, the proper place for them is the competent bodies." Prince Ali, who has been a vocal critic of FIFA's leadership, said he would make no further comment while the matter remained under consideration. The AFC did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on Prince Ali's latest post. Infantino, who has led FIFA since 2016, is seeking reelection in March after apologising for his abandoned proposal to sell a stake in FIFA competitions. The AFC's endorsement marked a sharp shift from its position three months earlier, when it accused FIFA of a "fundamental breach of trust" over the abandoned proposal. (Reporting Ashraf Hamed Atta;Editing by Peter Rutherford)

Source: Reuters

Oct 29 : STMicroelectronics reported a third-quarter operating profit above market expectations on Thursday, as demand from AI data centres and satellite operators added to a broader recovery in the chipmaker's markets. Operating income excluding one-off charges was $429 million, nearly doubling from a year ago and beating the $400.5 million expected by analysts polled by LSEG. The Franco-Italian chipmaker said it expected fourth-quarter revenue of $4.15 billion, up from $3.76 billion in the third quarter, give or take 3.5 per cent. Analysts polled by LSEG had expected $4.10 billion. "In an environment where demand remains well above supply, we continue to expand capacity aligned with ST's strategic roadmap," CEO Jean-Marc Chery said in the earnings statement.

STMicro, which makes chips ranging from microcontrollers to sensors and power semiconductors for cars, factories and smartphones, said higher sales of communication equipment, computer peripherals and personal electronics drove the beat. It had said already in July that fourth-quarter sales would be more than $4 billion. Chery said on Thursday that company-specific drivers, including AI data centre demand and low-Earth-orbit satellite communications, were adding to the cyclical recovery. The company's gross margin rose to 37.3 per cent in the third quarter from 33.2 per cent a year ago, helped by a higher share of sales from more profitable chips and lower costs from idle factory capacity. STMicro expects the margin to rise to about 39 per cent in the fourth quarter. Jefferies analysts expect STMicro's growth to continue into 2027, as data centre revenue is set to roughly double from this year to the next, while gross margins see "more significant upside towards the end of next year", they wrote in an early take on the report.

BHUBANESWAR: At least six people were killed and power supply in several areas along India's eastern coast remained disrupted on Thursday (Oct 29), one day after Cyclone Arnab barrelled through the region, bringing heavy rain and gusty winds, officials said. The Times of India newspaper, citing local officials, put the death toll at nine, caused by electrocution as well as tree and house collapses. The official death toll was six, an Andhra Pradesh state government official said. Cyclone Arnab, classified by the India Meteorological Department as a very severe cyclonic storm - the third-highest category on its scale - made landfall in Andhra Pradesh early on Wednesday.

A Marshall Island-flagged cargo vessel, with 20 crew members on board, that was grounded off the coast of Andhra Pradesh remained stalled on Thursday because of rough seas, officials said. More than 180,000 people had been evacuated in the states of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha ahead of the cyclone's arrival. Some schools were closed and some train and flight services cancelled. Arnab formed over the Bay of Bengal, a major region for tropical cyclones that has spawned deadly storms on India's east coast.

SEOUL: A Russian network of brokers sponsored by Pyongyang has taken North Koreans to work in Russia in exploitative conditions and in violation of United Nations sanctions, some at factories that turn out items Moscow uses in the Ukraine war, a rights group said. The neighbours have boosted military and political ties dramatically since pledging renewed cooperation at a 2023 summit of their leaders, while a mutual defence pact is a cornerstone of a partnership treaty signed the following year. In its report, the Hague-based group, Global Rights Compliance (GRC), said North Korea reaps funds from the operation, taking much of the wages earned by its workers who are sent to Russia and made to stay under threat of retribution. The group cites open source information on the operation run by a Russian businessman, facial recognition technology to identify North Korean officials, and evidence gathered by its members posing undercover as prospective employers.

"This investigation exposes a dangerous convergence between two states' military ambitions," said the group's legal adviser, Elise Lauriot Prevost. These were "North Korea's use of overseas forced labour to finance its weapons programme, and Russia's growing reliance on labour to sustain its war economy," she added.

Russia's foreign ministry and the North Korean embassy in Moscow did not respond to emails seeking comment. The rights group said it contacted two Russians identified as key figures in the network, but only one replied, denying the accusation. It did not say if the other responded. NORTH KOREA SENT TROOPS, SOUTH SAYS Since 2024, North Korea has sent more than 10,000 troops to fight alongside Russians in the Ukraine war, as well as weapons to replenish Moscow's dwindling armoury while gaining valuable battlefield experience, South Korea's intelligence agency has said. To evade UN sanctions that ban member nations from hiring North Korean workers, the latter enter Russia on student visas in the guise of enrolling at colleges, GRC said. Then they are contracted out to Russian employers, with brokers receiving a commission of up to 150,000 roubles (US$1,860) for each, it added. GRC investigators posed undercover as prospective employers and found the workers were hired at production sites, including a military rations factory. The workers are forced to stay on the job through coercion and threats of retribution against them and their families. One advertisement assured prospective employers that workers would not "run away," the report said. Workers labour 12-hour days with two days off each month, it added, citing such ads.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un shakes hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as they attend a ceremony to mark the 80th anniversary of the end of World War Two, in Beijing, China, in this picture released by the Korean Central News Agency on Sep 4, 2025. (File photo: Reuters)

After North Korea's sixth and last nuclear test in 2017, a UN Security Council resolution put a blanket ban on the hiring of its workers overseas and mandated their return home. Russia and China, two permanent members of the Security Council that voted for the ban, have since been accused by South Korea and the West of noncompliance with resolutions. Such measures, dating back to 2006, banned the flow of goods, energy, weapons and workers with North Korea. In previous years, Russia employed North Korean labourers in its far east while many North Koreans staffing restaurants in China sent home wages that were channelled to the state treasury, rights groups have said. North Korea is directly involved in running the network supplying workers in Russia, with officials from its Moscow embassy identified as inspecting work sites for prospective employment, the GRC report said. "These workers do not come cheap, yet little, if any, of the money paid for their labour reaches them," said Dyland Carter, a GRC lead investigator. "Instead, it lines the pockets of the DPRK state," he added, referring to North Korea by a short version of its official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

TOKYO, Oct 29 : Japanese government bonds (JGBs) were steady on Thursday, a day before the Bank of Japan's monetary policy decision, while strong demand at an auction of 2-year notes provided support. The market was also buoyed by gains in US Treasuries after the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged and gave few signals about the chances of a hike at the next meeting in December. "The market seemed to perceive it as less hawkish than expected," said Yuhi Kawano, a market analyst at Mizuho Securities. "Under these circumstances, it’s easy to see why the need for the Bank of Japan to raise rates at a high pace seems low, which should be supportive for the yen bond market."

• The benchmark 2-year JGB yield eased half a basis point to 1.895 per cent, reversing an earlier small rise following the auction results; yields fall when bond prices rise • A measure of demand called the bid-to-cover ratio rose to 4.03 at the 2-year auction, from 3.89 at a sale last month • The 10-year JGB yield also added 0.5 bp to 2.83 per cent, while the 5-year yield was flat at 2.265 per cent • The 30-year yield edged up half a basis point to 3.88 per cent; the 20-year JGB hadn't traded as of 0514 GMT • The BOJ is likely to leave rates unchanged on Friday and hike by a quarter-point in December, according to a Reuters poll of economists

Source: Reuters
